document.title: What should you put on your first marketing dashboard?

posts.content:
Most B2B SaaS product videos are just glorified screen recordings. Then there’s HubSpot.

Instead of showing dashboard clicks, they built video ads around the chaos of mismanaged data. They exaggerated real office pain points, made the videos relatable, and positioned their CRM as the ultimate sigh of relief.

The Revenue Impact: > According to data compiled in the HubSpot Marketing Statistics Report ((https://lnkd.in/eGck25aj), websites that integrate video hit an average conversion rate of 4.8%, compared to just 2.9% for sites that rely on static text alone. Furthermore, nearly 39% of marketers identify video as the single highest-impact element for landing page conversions.

The Teardown:

The 3-Second Rule: Ditch the animated company logo intro. Open immediately on the buyer's absolute worst daily operational bottleneck.
Agitate the Problem: Use relatable, slightly exaggerated humor or stress to build narrative tension around that bottleneck.
The Catharsis Moment: Introduce your product only after the problem's emotional peak. Your SaaS must feel like a breath of fresh air.
Micro-Demos over Feature Lists: Show 1 or 2 specific, high-value actions inside the UI. Do not try to explain the entire platform in one video.
Design for Silent Viewers: Burn text captions and explicit visual callouts directly into the video file. The vast majority of professional users scroll LinkedIn with sound muted.
The Aspect-Ratio Framework: Shoot the primary asset with enough framing cushion so it can be cropped seamlessly into 9:16 for paid social feeds and 16:9 for landing pages.

Check out the HubSpot YouTube Channel (youtube.com/hubspot) to see how they pace their product breakdowns.
